decisive_items: pain and swelling in both knees
diffusely swollen and tender to palpation
A plain radiograph of both knees was unremarkable
response.rationale: Bilateral knee involvement with elevated inflammatory markers but no fever and normal radiograph favors reactive arthritis (likely post-methotrexate or post-infection) over septic arthritis, which typically is monoarticular, febrile, and may show radiographic changes. Ectopic pregnancy is the underlying condition, not the current joint presentation.

rejected.why: No fever, bilateral symmetric involvement, and unremarkable radiograph argue against septic arthritis despite elevated inflammatory markers.
Ectopic pregnancy is the initial diagnosis and does not explain the new bilateral knee swelling and pain.
